concept.name: Chaikin oscillator
concept.definition: Marc Chaikin's momentum-of-money-flow oscillator: the MACD formula applied to the Accumulation/Distribution Line - the 3-day EMA of the ADL minus its 10-day EMA - designed to anticipate turns in accumulation and distribution.
concept.intuition: It is an indicator of an indicator: instead of watching the ADL's slow drift, you watch its momentum cross zero, flagging shifts in buying and selling pressure earlier.
concept.mechanics: Compute the ADL from Money Flow Multiplier times volume; the oscillator = EMA(ADL,3) - EMA(ADL,10). Positive means the ADL is rising (buying pressure), negative means it is falling; divergences with price warn of pressure shifts before zero-line confirmation.
concept.formula: Chaikin Oscillator = EMA(ADL, 3) - EMA(ADL, 10), with ADL the running sum of [((C-L) - (H-C)) / (H-L)] x V.
concept.failure_modes: Three derivations removed from price, it frequently disconnects from it, and the default (3,10) settings cross zero often, producing whipsaws that need confirmation.
concept.misconceptions: A bullish divergence is not yet buying pressure - while the oscillator stays below zero, selling pressure still dominates; confirmation requires a cross into positive territory.
concept.example: If the 3-day EMA of the ADL is 12,000 and the 10-day EMA is 11,000, the oscillator reads +1,000 - the threshold StockCharts uses in its bullish scan.
